---
title: "SSO Success Rate by Application"
description: "Share of SSO events that succeeded, by application."
---

The proportion of SSO events that succeeded, broken down by application.

This is the success rate of the handoff to an application, not of anyone signing
in. It helps isolate problems to a specific application: one with a markedly
lower success rate than its peers is worth investigating for integration or
configuration issues.

## Calculation

Divide the sum of `successful_logins` by the sum of all attempts
(`successful_logins + failed_logins`) over the selected reporting period, grouped
by application.

Group on `application_id`, not `application_name`: a partner can rename an
application, and the ID does not change. Each ID is labelled with its latest name
from
[`events_application_mapping`](../../catalog/ibm_verify_events_transformed/events_application_mapping.qmd).
The ID `UNKNOWN` marks events with no application and is left out.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
-- the latest name for each application ID
WITH latest_names AS (
    SELECT application_id, application_name
    FROM   ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_application_mapping
    WHERE  date = (
        SELECT MAX(date)
        FROM   ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_application_mapping
    )
)

SELECT
    a.application_id,
    n.application_name,
    CAST(SUM(a.successful_logins) AS DOUBLE)
        / NULLIF(SUM(a.successful_logins + a.failed_logins), 0) AS sso_success_rate
FROM ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_app_login_counts a
LEFT JOIN latest_names n ON a.application_id = n.application_id
-- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
WHERE CAST(a.from_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-05-28'
  AND a.application_id <> 'UNKNOWN'
-- optionally filter out internal CanadaLogin components;
-- see the note on them in cookbook/notes.qmd
  AND a.application_id NOT IN (
      SELECT al.alias
      FROM   rp.alias al
      JOIN   rp.service s ON al.rp_id = s.rp_id
      WHERE  s.is_internal
  )
GROUP BY a.application_id, n.application_name
ORDER BY sso_success_rate DESC;
```

## R

```r
latest_names <- tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_application_mapping")) |>
  filter(date == max(date, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  select(application_id, application_name)

internal_apps <- tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "alias")) |>
  inner_join(tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "service")), by = "rp_id") |>
  filter(is_internal) |>
  select(application_id = alias)

tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_app_login_counts")) |>
  # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  filter(
    as.Date(from_date) >= as.Date("2026-01-01"),
    as.Date(from_date) <= as.Date("2026-05-28"),
    application_id != "UNKNOWN"
  ) |>
  # optionally filter out internal CanadaLogin components;
  # see the note on them in cookbook/notes.qmd
  anti_join(internal_apps, by = "application_id") |>
  # the table also holds the name seen that day; keep only the latest
  select(-application_name) |>
  left_join(latest_names, by = "application_id") |>
  group_by(application_id, application_name) |>
  summarise(
    sso_success_rate =
      sum(as.double(successful_logins), na.rm = TRUE) /
        sum(successful_logins + failed_logins, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(sso_success_rate))
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

Compare applications against each other rather than
against an absolute target. This measures the handoff to a relying party after the
person has already signed in to CanadaLogin. The person enters no password and no
second factor; the check is whether the session can be used for that application. It
counts a different IBM Verify event type from the CanadaLogin-wide
[authentication success rate](sign-in-success-rate.qmd), so the two are not
comparable.

## Alternative names

- application handoff success rate
- single sign-on success rate by application
- per-application sign-in success rate
